tests.name: Cardio C-Reactive Protein (hsCRP)
tests.finding: At the boundary of low cardiovascular risk
tests.explanation: hsCRP is a marker of inflammation that helps gauge cardiovascular risk. A value of 1.00 mg/L sits right at the boundary between the low-risk (<1) and average-risk (1–3) bands shown on the report. Repeating the test in a few weeks is commonly recommended to confirm the trend.

tests.name: Apolipoprotein B (Apo B)
tests.finding: Right at the lower end of normal
tests.explanation: Apo B reflects the number of cholesterol-carrying particles linked to atherosclerosis. This result is just inside the lower edge of the printed reference range, which is generally a favorable signal.

tests.name: Troponin-I, High Sensitive
tests.range: <6 (male, low risk cut-off shown on report)
tests.finding: Within the low-risk band for males
tests.explanation: High-sensitivity Troponin-I helps detect cardiac stress. The reading of 4 ng/L falls under the report's low-risk cut-off of <6 for males, which is reassuring.
tests.source_snippet: TROPONIN- I, SERUM  HIGH SENSITIVE  (CMIA)  ng/L 4

tests.name: Glucose, Fasting (Plasma)
tests.explanation: The fasting glucose value has not been reported yet on this interim report. The reference range is shown for context.

tests.name: HbA1c (Glycosylated Hemoglobin)
tests.explanation: HbA1c gives an estimate of average blood sugar over the past few months. The numeric result is not yet reported on this interim report.
tests.source_snippet: HbA1c (GLYCOSYLATED HEMOGLOBIN), BLOOD  (HPLC, NGSP certified)  HbA1c   %   4.00 - 5.60

summary: This is an interim Heart Health Screen. hsCRP sits right at the boundary between low and average cardiovascular risk; Apo B and Troponin-I are within the printed reference ranges. Several panel results (lipids, glucose, HbA1c, Lp(a)) have not been reported yet.
